title: [CQ-R13a] Linux prerequisites cache directory
description:
Objective: let `node scripts/local-runner/cli.mjs prerequisites` reach exit 0 on a correctly provisioned Linux host, and pin the provider-precedence rule that QA found unguarded. Both are QA relays from CQ-R04 (task-120b6a11), posted on CQ-R13 by the governor on 2026-10-25.

Split out of CQ-R13 (task-f4811a72) by architect-e4b7eee0 on 2026-10-30. The human decided in the architect REPL that certification-gating items become CQ-R rows before R13. This row depends on CQ-R11e (task-001d8ab3), the last planned editor of scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs before it.

Why: hostPrerequisites passes no cacheDir. platform-linux.mjs cacheReadable returns null for an undefined cacheDir, because the snap's home plug reads only paths strictly below home with no hidden segment. So the Linux report is never ready, and the command always fails closed.

Deliverable:
- cli.mjs: `prerequisites` accepts `--cache-dir <absolute path>` beside `--executable <path>`.
  - Each flag is optional and allowed at most once, in either order.
  - hostPrerequisites({ executable, cacheDir }) passes it on as platform.prerequisites({ provider: { executable }, cacheDir }).
  - A relative, empty, control-character or repeated flag is CLI_INPUT_INVALID.
  - USAGE names the flag; `doctor` and `native-smoke` are unchanged.
- hostPrerequisites gains a test-only second argument, { platform = platformFor(process.platform) }.
- Tests in scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs:
  - argument parsing rows;
  - an end-to-end row: runCli with a Linux platform whose prerequisite seams (doctor, snap, kvm, cpus, memory, disk, homedir) all hold, and a cache directory strictly under home with no hidden segment, gives ready:true and exit 0. The same host without --cache-dir gives exit 2;
  - a provisionGuest row: an explicit provider.executable is used for every provider call instead of platform.executable.

Out of scope:
- platform rule changes;
- provisioning;
- any verified-local or isolation claim;
- .moe edits.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0 required): node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs (on WSL: env -i with the nvm Node 24 PATH)
definitionOfDone: `prerequisites --cache-dir <absolute path>` passes that directory to the host platform's prerequisites, alone or with `--executable`, in either order. A relative, empty, control-character or repeated flag is CLI_INPUT_INVALID. Shown by tests.

Through runCli, a Linux host whose every prerequisite holds, with a cache directory strictly under home and no hidden segment, reports ready:true and exits 0. The same host without --cache-dir still exits 2. Shown by an end-to-end test with seamed Linux prerequisites.
provisionGuest uses an explicit provider.executable for every provider call instead of the platform's default client. Shown by a test.
The verification command exits 0 with its output supplied to complete_task.

implementationPlan.description:
scripts/local-runner/cli.mjs, from its LANDED bytes.

1. Replace argumentsFor with one table-driven parser. Its behavior for doctor and native-smoke must stay identical:
   const FLAGS = { doctor: {'--executable': 'executable'}, prerequisites: {'--executable': 'executable', '--cache-dir': 'cacheDir'}, 'native-smoke': {'--work-dir': 'workDir'} }
   - argv must be an array, argv[0] an own key of FLAGS (use Object.hasOwn, never a plain lookup), and argv.length odd.
   - Read (flag, value) pairs in order. Each pair is refused (null) when:
     - the flag is not an own key of that command's table;
     - the flag's option was already set;
     - the value is not a string, is blank after trim, or holds a control character (/[\x00-\x1f\x7f]/);
     - the option is cacheDir or workDir and !path.isAbsolute(value).
   - native-smoke without workDir is null.
   - Return {command, options}, where options holds only the flags given.
   This keeps every existing CLI row green: a bare doctor or prerequisites, --executable, native-smoke --work-dir, and each existing refusal.
2. USAGE = 'Usage: cli.mjs doctor [--executable <path>] | prerequisites [--executable <path>] [--cache-dir <absolute path>] | native-smoke --work-dir <absolute path>'.
3. Change the signature to:
   export async function hostPrerequisites({ executable, cacheDir } = {}, { platform = platformFor(process.platform) } = {})
   It calls platform.prerequisites({ provider: { executable }, cacheDir }) and keeps its result mapping and its PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED branch. The default runs per call, so the existing unsupported-host row (which swaps process.platform) still works. The JSDoc says platform is a test seam. vm-control.mjs's prerequisites({}) call is unaffected.
4. runCli, reportFor, smokeReport and the doctor path are unchanged. The parsed options object goes to prerequisites exactly as today.

Error handling: every malformed argv is CLI_INPUT_INVALID with USAGE, before any doctor or prerequisites call. A throwing prerequisites call is still PREREQUISITES_UNAVAILABLE, with no stack or path in the report. No platform rule changes: cacheReadable still decides what a usable cache directory is.

Then `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs` must be green.
implementationPlan.note: Table-driven parser + hostPrerequisites platform seam; full local-runner.test.mjs green (293/292/0/1 skip).

executionContract.intendedBehavior: `node scripts/local-runner/cli.mjs prerequisites` takes an optional `--cache-dir <absolute path>` beside the optional `--executable <path>`. Each flag may appear at most once, in either order. hostPrerequisites passes the directory to the host platform as platform.prerequisites({provider: {executable}, cacheDir}), so a correctly provisioned Linux host with a cache directory strictly under home, with no hidden segment, reports ready:true and exits 0. Without the flag it still exits 2. A malformed flag is CLI_INPUT_INVALID before any prerequisite call. doctor and native-smoke accept exactly what they did before. hostPrerequisites gains a test-only {platform} second argument. A test pins that provisionGuest sends every Multipass call to an explicit provider.executable rather than the platform's default client.
acceptanceCriteria: Rejection rows: a relative, empty, blank, control-character, repeated or dangling --cache-dir, plus doctor or native-smoke given --cache-dir, are each CLI_INPUT_INVALID with the new USAGE, with zero prerequisite calls and exit 2.

Pass-through row: --cache-dir alone, or with --executable in either order, reaches prerequisites as exactly {cacheDir} or {executable, cacheDir}. hostPrerequisites forwards exactly {provider: {executable}, cacheDir} to the platform seam.

End-to-end Linux row: with --cache-dir /home/u/moe-images, every seamed prerequisite holds and the run exits 0 with LINUX_READY. Without the flag it exits 2 with the cache item null. With a hidden cache dir it exits 2 with the cache item false. With --executable, the doctor calls use it.
provisionGuest row: with an explicit provider.executable, every non-snap call uses it and the snap's /snap/bin/multipass is never called.
invariants: No platform rule changes: platform-linux.mjs cacheReadable alone decides whether a cache directory is usable.
Every malformed argv is refused before any doctor or prerequisites call, with only the fixed CLI_INPUT_INVALID report.
doctor and native-smoke accept exactly the argv they accepted before.
Reports carry no stack, path or provider diagnostic beyond the existing fields. No .moe edits. No verified-local or isolation claim.
compatibility: vm-control.mjs statusReport calls hostPrerequisites({}), which keeps working through the defaulted first argument and the default platform.
Windows and macOS platforms get cacheDir passed through and apply their own rules; the Windows module ignores it.
The CLI's JSON report shapes and exit codes are unchanged except that a ready Linux host can now reach 0.

sourceAssumptions: cli.mjs argumentsFor accepts [cmd], [cmd, '--executable', x] (doctor and prerequisites) or ['native-smoke', '--work-dir', abs]. hostPrerequisites({executable}) calls platformFor(process.platform).prerequisites({provider: {executable}}).

platform-linux.mjs cacheReadable(cacheDir, home) is null for an undefined cacheDir, false for a relative, hidden or outside-home directory, and true strictly under home. prerequisites() takes provider, cacheDir, doctor, snapExecutable, statDevice, statfs, cpus, freemem, homedir and host seams.
provision.mjs provisionGuest sets provider = {...provider, executable: provider.executable ?? platform.executable} before the prerequisites call and every provider call.
vm-control.mjs statusReport calls prerequisites({}) with prerequisites defaulting to hostPrerequisites.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- A table-driven argv parser (FLAGS per command), chosen over a fourth special case in the old argumentsFor. It is about the same size, makes 'either order, at most once' structural, and keeps doctor and native-smoke byte-for-byte equivalent.
- The platform seam is the second argument of hostPrerequisites, as the description asks. Keeping process.platform swapping was rejected; the existing unsupported-host row still swaps it and keeps working, because the default is evaluated per call.
- The provisionGuest row covers Linux only: the QA relay concerned the Linux snap pin. Windows keeps its own default-client row.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- local-runner.test.mjs already has complete Linux seams (ROOMY, with homedir /home/u and cacheDir /home/u/moe-images) plus a provisioning harness with linuxVm, which records each call's executable.
- ROOMY passes host: LINUX_HOST and cacheReadable uses path.posix, so the end-to-end CLI row runs on every CI OS. The provisionGuest row composes POSIX host paths and skips on win32, like its neighbours.
- USAGE appears only in cli.mjs and the test's own copy at about line 2116; no doc quotes it.
- CQ-R13d (task-a8a3a502) adds `certify` to cli.mjs next and depends on this task.
planningNotes.risks:
- The test file is large and shared. CQ-R11e (dependsOn) lands its CJ rows first; edit only the CLI and Linux sections.
- path.isAbsolute follows the host's syntax: '/home/u/...' counts as absolute on Windows too, so the rows stay portable.
- The global forbiddenPatterns include the prototype-accessor key name: never write that literal in code or tests. Use 'constructor', 'toString' and 'hasOwnProperty' for the prototype-key probes.
- The shared checkout carries other sessions' dirty paths. Report only the two files.
